requirement:
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the
combined coverage totals. Their retained per-process reports MUST remain
inspectable using their captured source until the build artifacts are removed.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. I reasoned from the supplied test source only and did not request implementation source.

**Obligation 1: only matching source and compatible builds contribute counts.**
- `src/execution_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_and_build_inputs_invalidate_on_addition_removal_and_dirty_content]` checks the `fresh` predicate directly. A matching run is fresh. It becomes stale when any of these happens:
  - a source file's content changes;
  - a Rust file is added;
  - `Cargo.lock` or `Cargo.toml` changes, or either is removed;
  - a member `Cargo.toml` or a `rust-toolchain.toml` appears;
  - a new or nested file appears in a watched input directory;
  - a previously absent watched path is created;
  - a captured source file is removed.
  After each change it restores the original state and asserts the run is fresh again.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cargo_launch_metadata_does_not_invalidate_but_caller_build_environment_does]` covers build-configuration compatibility through the environment. Cargo launch metadata variables do not make a record stale. Changes to `CC`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_PROFILE_*`, a target linker variable and a custom build input each render "stale: source inputs changed or unavailable".
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[real_build_captures_dependency_files_and_environment_for_read_only_freshness_checks]` is an end-to-end test with a real build.
  - It checks that included files, build-script inputs, `Cargo.lock`, and compiler and build environment values are captured.
  - Changing an included file or a rerun-if-changed file marks the record stale. Changing either environment value does too.
  - Restoring the files makes the record fresh again.
  - The retained files are unchanged after rendering, which fits the read-only expectation.
- `book.rs#fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` adds a newer record under a different build configuration, `build-b`. The page shows "historical build configuration" and totals of 1/1. The older `build-a` records therefore do not contribute.

**Obligation 2: stale or unavailable records are identified and excluded from totals.**
- The same filtered-runs test changes `code.rs`. It asserts that the page shows "gap counts unavailable" and "stale: source inputs changed or unavailable".
- `book.rs#fn[incomplete_attempts_do_not_label_their_files_as_unmeasured_in_a_partial_map]` makes one run stale while another run stays fresh. The page shows "Coverage unavailable", no per-file map, and "1 stale test attempts". A stale record therefore does not leak partial counts into the totals.
- `book.rs#fn[unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success]` covers the unavailable cases. In each one the page shows "gap counts unavailable" or "unavailable: …" and does not show the older success's "1/1 (100.0%)":
  - unreadable `attempt.json`;
  - missing captured sources;
  - unsupported schema, which means compatibility cannot be established;
  - a missing raw profile.

**Obligation 3: retained per-process reports stay inspectable using captured source.**
- In the stale scenario of the filtered-runs test, the assertion `chapters().any(... contains("fn one() {}"))` shows the captured source is still rendered after the live source changed.
- The unreadable-history test checks that a per-process chapter still explains why it is unavailable, for example "Matching captured source is missing" and "A retained raw profile is missing".
- The "until build artifacts are removed" limit is a lifetime bound. It does not call for a separate test.

**Possible weakness, not a gap.** In the stale scenarios the tests assert "gap counts unavailable" and "Coverage unavailable" but do not always assert that a specific count string is absent. The unavailable-totals indication is the observable form of exclusion, so I don't treat this as a gap.

All tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, and I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} index.freshness
Only records whose captured source inputs match the current project source and
whose build configurations are compatible MAY contribute execution counts to
the combined view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`.
Records invalidated by a source change, or whose compatibility cannot be
established, MUST be identified as stale or unavailable and excluded from the

:::{req} index.selection
The coverage index MUST combine the most recent recorded test attempt for each
nextest binary and test name among the retained runs. "Most recent" MUST refer
to when the attempt started, including failed or interrupted attempts. A newer
filtered run MUST update only the tests it executes, leaving other compatible
test records available to the combined view. A newer attempt with missing or
unreadable coverage MUST be shown as unavailable rather than replaced with an
older successful attempt. Results from incompatible instrumented build
configurations MUST NOT be combined under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.configuration`.
The main combined view MUST use the instrumented build configuration of the
most recently started recorded test attempt. Latest-per-test selection MUST
occur within that configuration. Records from other configurations MUST be
identified as excluded historical coverage. Configuration selection MUST use
recorded metadata without building or executing tests.
